title: Palais des Beaux-Arts de Lille: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty pictures in which a raised hand, a turned head or an ordinary pause changes the scale of the subject.
introduction:
In David's *Belisarius*, a soldier recognises a fallen general while a woman offers help. The gestures make a public history intelligible through a small encounter. Elsewhere in this selection, a crowd lifts Marat above its heads, two women lean together in confidence, and a sleeping girl withdraws from activity altogether.

These scenes do not ask for the same kind of attention. Some announce their subject through a conspicuous action; others require time with an almost uneventful arrangement. Even the landscapes alternate between directed movement and stillness. The guide follows those differences across twenty collection works, leaving their historical reputations in the background long enough to notice what each picture actually gives its figures to do.

books.title: Seven Discourses on Art
books.author: Joshua Reynolds
books.note: Reynolds's Seven Discourses on Art records an influential eighteenth-century argument about the ambitions of painting. It offers a historical counterpoint to the large figure compositions by David and Delacroix, rather than a commentary on these particular works.

works.title: Belisarius Begging for Alms
works.credit: Belisarius Begging for Alms. WikiArt; Jacques-Louis David. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The helmet no longer protects its wearer; it receives charity. Around this reversal, David assigns distinct actions to the boy, the approaching woman and the astonished soldier. The blind general cannot share their act of recognition. His dependence is made visible through the different kinds of knowledge and assistance held by the people around him.

works.title: Five Studies of Cows
works.credit: Jacob Jordaens. Five studies of cows. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/jacob-jordaens/five-studies-of-cows-1624
works.description: These cattle occupy one surface without becoming a single continuous scene. Standing and resting bodies offer Jordaens different problems of weight, overlap and the turn of a head. The repetitions preserve the practical character of a study. A familiar animal must still be observed anew when its position changes; one successful outline cannot do every job.

works.title: The Triumph of Marat
works.medium: Oil on white paper mounted on canvas
works.credit: Louis-Léopold Boilly. Le triomphe de Marat. Image credit: Louis-Léopold Boilly; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lille_PBA_boilly_triomphe_de_marat.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Marat's elevation is literal: the crowd carries him. Raised arms and clustered heads make public importance visible as collective behaviour rather than as a quality inherent in the central body. Boilly gives the surrounding people much of the picture's work. Remove their coordinated attention and the figure above them would lose the conditions of his triumph.

works.title: Medea
works.credit: Medea. WikiArt; Eugène Delacroix. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The close grouping might initially resemble protection: an adult holds two children within a rocky shelter. Medea's turned head and tense grip prevent that arrangement from becoming secure. Knowledge of the myth makes the children's dependence especially troubling. Delacroix concentrates the threat inside bodily contact rather than placing danger at a reassuring distance from the family.

works.title: Robespierre
works.credit: Louis-Léopold Boilly. Portrait de Maximilien Robespierre. Image credit: Louis-Léopold Boilly; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lille_PBA_Boilly_robespierre.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Papers, a desk and orderly clothing present a composed civilian sitter. It is tempting to search the face for a later political reputation, but the portrait does not supply evidence for that retrospective judgment. Boilly's restrained arrangement is more useful as an account of presentation: the sitter appears through the conventions of a particular kind of formal likeness.

works.title: Study for the Race of the Barbary Horses
works.catalogueTitle: Study for the Race of the Barbarian Horses
works.credit: Study for the Race of the Barbarian Horses. WikiArt; Théodore Géricault. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The horse is being held, not yet released. Géricault concentrates on the unstable interval in which human limbs and the animal's neck pull in competing directions. Closely packed bodies make it difficult to isolate a single action. Restraint becomes visible as continuous effort, and the anticipated race is already present in the forces resisting that effort.

works.title: After the Thaw: The Seine at the Pont de Suresnes
works.catalogueTitle: APRES LA DEBACLE LA SEINE AU PONT DE SURESNES
works.credit: Alfred Sisley. APRES LA DEBACLE LA SEINE AU PONT DE SURESNES. Image credit: Alfred Sisley; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lille_PdBA_sisley_apres_la_debacle.JPG. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The river occupies an unusually broad, pale area beside the wet bank. Small walkers make its width measurable without taking over the scene. Sisley allows a change in weather to alter the landscape's proportions: water claims space that might otherwise belong to firm ground. The result depends on those changed boundaries more than on an isolated picturesque detail.

works.title: Apelles Painting Campaspe in the Presence of Alexander
works.catalogueTitle: Apelle peignant Campaspe en présence d'Alexandre
works.credit: Jacques-Louis David. Apelle peignant Campaspe en présence d'Alexandre. Image credit: Sailko; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Jacques-louis_david,_apelle_ritrae_camaspe_alla_presenza_di_alessandro,_1813-23_ca.jpg. CC BY 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The easel divides an encounter involving a painter, a model and a ruler. Each occupies a different relation to the image being made. David turns an ancient subject into a painting about access and attention: the model is looked at, the painter works, and the visitor observes. The canvas stands between those activities rather than disappearing behind the story.

works.title: Travellers in a Rocky Landscape
works.credit: David Teniers the Younger. BOHEMIENS. Image credit: David Teniers the Younger; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lille_PdBA_tenier_jeune_bohemiens.JPG. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The travellers are small enough to make the rocks formidable. Their route nevertheless introduces a passage through terrain that first appears obstructive. Teniers balances enclosure with a prospect of open country, allowing the eye to alternate between following the path and looking beyond it. The people establish both scale and the possibility of movement.

works.title: Bouquet of Flowers
works.credit: Roelant Savery. BOUQUET DE FLEURS. Image credit: Roelant Savery; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lille_PdBA_savery_bouquet_de_fleurs.JPG. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The bouquet's crowded centre does not erase the differences between its flowers. Savery gives individual stems and delicate edges enough contrast against the dark ground to remain legible. Fallen blossoms extend the arrangement beyond the vase. The painting offers a useful distinction between abundance and uniformity: many forms share the space without becoming one indistinct mass.

works.title: Brie-sur-Marne
works.credit: Stanislas Lépine. BRIE-SUR-MARNE. Image credit: Stanislas Lépine; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lille_PdBA_lepine_brie_sur_marne.JPG. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The inhabited bank has a second, less solid existence in the water. Lépine organises river, houses and sky into broad horizontal zones, then allows their reflections to loosen the division. Little appears to happen, but looking between a building and its reflected counterpart produces small changes of shape. Stillness is not the same as exact repetition.

works.title: A Shepherd from the Landes
works.credit: Rosa Bonheur. Berger Landais. Image credit: Rosa Bonheur; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lille_Pdba_bonheur_berger_landais.JPG. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Bonheur brings the shepherd close enough for the rough outer garment to matter alongside the face. The dark cap and blue sky clarify the turned head, while the cropping removes a larger account of rural work. Occupation remains present in clothing and bearing. The worker receives the concentrated attention of a portrait rather than serving as a small landscape accessory.

works.title: Pug with a Red Ribbon
works.credit: Jean-Baptiste Oudry. CARLIN PARE D'UN RUBAN ROUGE. Image credit: Jean-Baptiste Oudry; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lille_PdBA_oudry_carlin.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The ribbon introduces a bright accent at the neck, but the dog's stance carries the image. Oudry sets the compact pale body against darker surroundings so that its open mouth and alert position remain distinct. An animal portrait need not imitate a human sitter's dignity. Attention to the creature's particular proportions supplies its own terms.

works.title: Wheat Field
works.credit: Jacob van Ruisdael. CHAMP DE BLE. Image credit: Jacob van Ruisdael; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lille_PdBA_Van_Ruisdael_champ_de_ble.JPG. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The curved path proposes a journey through cultivated ground, while the large cloud banks claim another kind of scale above it. Ruisdael places small travellers between these competing expanses. Their route makes the terrain continuous and traversable, but the sky prevents the fields from feeling wholly controlled by human activity. Cultivation and weather occupy the same view.

works.title: Confidence
works.medium: Oil on canvas mounted on wood
works.credit: Jules Breton. Trust. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/jules-breton/trust-1864
works.description: One young woman leans towards the other, bringing their bodies into a shared direction. Breton makes the relationship readable while withholding the content of the exchange. The surrounding space remains available, yet the pair's closeness marks a smaller private area within it. There is no need to invent their conversation to recognise the intimacy of its arrangement.

works.title: Pear Pickers
works.credit: Émile Bernard. CUEILLEUSES DE POIRES. Image credit: Émile Bernard; Self-photographed. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lille_PdBA_emile_bernard_cueilleuses_de_poires.JPG. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Dark contours give the coloured areas boundaries that do not depend on naturalistic shadow. Bernard keeps figures and trees identifiable while compressing their depth. Each patch has a weight in the surface arrangement as well as a role in describing the scene. Following the outlines makes that double function easier to notice than searching for a single convincing viewpoint.

works.title: The Old Women, or Time
works.credit: Francisco Goya. Les vieilles ou Le temps. Image credit: Francisco Goya; Own work , Chatsam , 2015-07-05 11:41:15. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Goya_le_temps_pdba_lille.JPG. CC BY-SA 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The mirror offers a small field of self-inspection, while the winged figure and raised broom introduce a larger threat behind the women. Goya does not allow elegant clothing to settle the encounter into a flattering portrait. The picture places the wish to manage appearance beside an image of passing time that appearance cannot control.

works.title: In the Woods
works.credit: Albert Anker. DANS LES BOIS. Image credit: Albert Anker; Joconde database :  entry 000PE019295. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Albert_Anker_-_Im_Wald.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Cut branches locate the sleeping girl near work, but the painting concentrates on its suspension. A hand supports her head as the wooded ground encloses the body. Anker makes an unposed interval available to sustained looking. The scene does not establish a full account of her circumstances; the visible contrast is between signs of activity and present rest.

works.title: Erigone
works.credit: Gustave Moreau. ERIGONE. Image credit: Gustave Moreau; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lille_Pdba_moreau_erigone.JPG. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The pale body emerges from a setting that remains difficult to separate into clear parts. Moreau gives small areas of light the task of distinguishing skin from the dense growth and shadow around it. The mythological name does not immediately clarify the space. Identifying the subject and finding one's way through the picture remain different kinds of reading.

works.title: Winter: Snow Effect
works.credit: Alfred Sisley. En hiver effet de neige. Image credit: Patrice78500; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:En_hiver,_effet_de_neige,_Alfred_Sisley.jpg. CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Snow reduces strong local colours without removing the road's structure. Grey and violet shadows interrupt the white, while converging edges carry carriages and walkers between houses and trees. Sisley gives the soft conditions a definite direction. The scene can remain subdued in colour and still contain a clearly organised pattern of everyday movement.

closingSections.title: Leave room for a quiet picture
paragraphs: After the dramatic groups, allow time for Lépine's river or Sisley's snow. The difference in pace is part of this selection. Consult the museum's current information for availability; these works are not promised in a single route or display.
